spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation
 of the Chapter


---


**
¶1.
** There
 are those
 among us who
 say
 that the Divine wills the
 existence of the external natural
 human.
 They
 reason
 thus
: The
 proce
eding Divine
 Wisdom projected the
 form of its
 own order
 into the natural mind, and the self
-derived faculties of
 that
 mind
 —
 its
 ruling
 loves
 and governing
 powers
 — perceived this form and shaped the external
 human after its likeness,
 which
 are
 the
 will
 and the
 understanding in
 their
 merely
 natural state
. See
, then, they
 say, the Divine cons
ents to this
,
 for
 it has
 made
 its
 order
 visible
 to
 the
 self
-derived faculties,
 and they have constructed accordingly
. Had
 the Divine not willed the natural
 human
, it would never
 have unc
overed its form, nor would the
 self-derived powers
 have fashioned human
 nature
 after its likeness.

---


**¶2.** But regarding
 the proce
eding Divine Wisdom:
 when
 it descended
 and made
 itself perceptible in the natural mind
, it did
 not come in
 order to reveal its form to the self
-derived faculties of
 that mind. Rather, it came and
 made itself manifest
 because
 of the
 interior spiritual life and
 the interior divine truth —
 its
 own
 ind
welling good
 — which
 was
 dispers
ed throughout
 every
 state
,
 that
 it might restore
 it to life
 and accomplish
 its liberation
,
 and free
 what
 is spiritual
 from every bond of
 falsity and every
 f
etter of
 evil desire
 in
 which
 it was
 entangled and
 held
 capt
ive.

---

**¶
3.** Still
, consider
 this: the self
-derived faculties and
 governing
 powers of
 the natural mind, having no genuine form
 of their own, coveted the form
 of Divine
 Wisdom when
 they
 perceived it. They reflected
 upon themselves and
 recognized
 that nothing
 in
 their own
 creation resembled it
. They im
printed this perceived form upon their will
 and upon
 their understanding.
 Afterward they
 constructed the external human after its
 likeness —
 the
 natural
 will
 and natural
 understanding.
 They
 sealed
 the
 image of the Divine
 within
 themselves
. And
 so they produced
 an
 imitation;
 but they did
 not reproduce
 it in truth. For
 what
 they
 fash
ioned came
 from
 themselves
, and
 though
 it out
wardly resembles the
 Divine order
, it does
 not in
wardly correspond to it.
 So
 too is the
 external
 form
 of the
 natural human:
 it was
 copied
 against the pattern
 of the Divine, but it is not
 that
 pattern in
 reality
.

---

**¶4
.** Similarly with
 perception
 itself
 — for
 while
 it outwardly resembles genuine spiritual
 perception, it has
 not
 been repro
duced in truth.


---

**¶5.
** This matter may
 be understood
 through
 the following
 lik
eness: There
 is a pure
 and
 noble
 wisdom,
 free
 in
 its origin
, dwelling
 within
 the inmost states of heaven, rich
 in all spiritual goods and
 poss
essions, beautiful in the radiance of
 its
 truth, and virt
uous in its holiness. It
 moves
 in a free and ex
alted state
. The fame
 of its beauty has spread through
 every province
 of the mind,
 sur
passing all else
. Within
 its inmost chamber, the
 n
oblest aff
ections and the
 highest
 loves
 desire to behold its
 beauty. Yet
 they
 cannot
 reach
 it, for
 it remains
 hidden within its celest
ial dwelling
.
 Now
 this
 pure
 wisdom does
 not come forth
 from its
 inmost state into the external world of
 its
 own accord or
 for
 the sake of display
. But
 when
 its
 beloved
 —
 the interior good
 that is its
 own
 life
 — is in
 suffering, then
 this
 wisdom leaves
 its in
most chamber and comes into
 the open
,
 into
 the midst
 of all
 states
 of mind
, and reveals
 its
 face and its beauty, solely
 because of its
 beloved
.
 This wisdom
, upon
 which no merely
 natural faculty
 had
 ever looked, and
 whose
 inner
 quality
 no
 one
 had ever perceived
, neither
 des
iring nor del
ighting in
 out
ward display
 —
 it leaves
 its interior
 state
 behind
 and comes into the midst of the
 human
 mind
 so
 that all
 may
 be
hold it:
 the noble
 aff
ections and the honor
able thoughts
, and
 even
 the lowest
 servants
 of
 the natural
 mind, all
 look
 upon it.

---

**
¶6.** In accordance
 with this lik
eness: this
 too is how the proceeding Divine
 Wisdom acts
.
 As
 this pure wisdom does
 not come forth
 in
 w
antonness or
 pride, nor does
 it consent to the outer world for the
 outer
 world's sake, it reveals its form
 and
 its beauty only under the compulsion of
 grief and love for what is beloved and
 suffering within.

---

**
¶7.** This,
 then, is the
 way of
 the proceeding Divine Truth
 in
 its third
 operation
:
 when it descended
 and displayed
 the
 form of divine
 order
 before
 all the powers
 of the natural mind. It did not
 come so that all
 the self
-derived fac
ulties and
 governing authorities
 would sculpt an external form
 after its likeness. Rather, it
 came because its own
 interior truth was
 crucified — that is, dispersed
 and suffering throughout every level of the natural
 mind — so
 that it might release that
 truth,
 free it, and rescue it from opp
ression. Yet
 when the self
-derived faculties beheld this form
, they coveted its
 beauty.
 They fashioned the natural
 will
 and natural
 understanding —
 the external human — after
 its
 likeness, without the consent
 of the Divine itself
.

---

**¶9
.**
 Understand also this further
 teaching
: Just
 as the natural will
 and understanding
 were
 fashioned by
 the self-derived faculties and stam
ped after
 the form
 of the Divine, so too a
 mult
itude of intermediate
 spiritual powers and angelic intellig
ences received the im
press of that form when
 it was displayed to
 them. For
 in the majesty of its wisdom and
 the warmth of its love, they
 burned with lon
ging and were und
one by
 their
 own
 desire —
 like one who ga
zes upon a beauty
 beyond
 compreh
ension and is consumed by the force
 of that
 desire
.

---

**¶10
.** This is also the case with
 those powers:
 when they beheld that
 majestic and beautiful form of
 divine order
, they received its stamp
. They copied it in likeness at
 every successive
 degree
 of descent — and
 what
 they copied was made
 into
 forms
 at
 each
 level
, even
 down to the lowest and most fixed natural
 tru
ths,
 the
 very
 foundations
 of the
 mind
 —
 from state to state. The form of
 divine order that
 was displayed in the natural world left its
 im
press and its
 stamp throughout all degrees of existence
,
 being
 received
 and
 revealed at
 every level.

---

**
¶11.** Now, the
 new formation that was
 brought
 forth in
 this new
 manner
 in
 the world — the natural
 will and natural understanding — is
 unlike
 anything
 that had existed in those
 lower states of mind since the beginning.
 No such form had ever appeared
 in the lower degrees
,
 because the image of divine order had never
 before descended to those depths.

---


**¶12.** Not
 all the forms that
 have
 been fashioned in
 the mind were fashioned through
 the open conjunction of higher wisdom
 with
 lower reception
. Rather
, there
 are other forms that
 arose
 by
 different
 means.

---

**¶
13.** The
 first of
 these is
 a monstrous falsity dwelling
 in the sensory mind — a
 swe
eping dist
urb
ance cast
 from
 the outermost boundary of heaven by
 the Divine source of all
 life into the aggregate of natural knowledge.
 Its own self-love and its
 own
 perverted reasoning
 shaped
 it into a distinct and
 terrible
 form.

---

**¶
14.** The second form
 is
 one
 that fell into
 the natural mind and made the sensory
 level of
 knowledge
 its generative ground. Its own perv
erted desire became its sculptor. By
 itself alone
 it
 fash
ioned itself into a nature that is the
 root of spiritual death. And
 when it arose from the sensory level
, it sought to destroy all
 the works of spiritual life. Immediately
, the invincible power
 of Divine
 Truth — the great instruction of spiritual strength
 — was sent against it. It was
 subdued and
 hum
bled in the ou
termost states of obscurity and ignor
ance. It is held underfoot and
 pressed
 down until the cons
ummation of the age
.

---

**¶15
.** The third form is a nature
 that fell upon the receptive ground of
 the natural mind itself
.
 It fashioned itself into a fixed
 perception
 and established itself there —
 a new
 form generated
 not
 from
 above
 but from the
 ground
 of
 natural
 existence
.

---

**¶16
.** In
 their
 essence
, all these forms share in the nature
 of falsity and spiritual
 darkness
. Yet
 they did not descend with the supreme
 ruling
 evil
 into
 the world. Rather, their
 fashioning came about subsequently
 — they are composite states
,
 mix
tures of truth and falsity, and
 they have been made manifest in the natural
 world as
 such
.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Regarding the Ambassador, the occasion when he came displaying his image, he [d]id not come so th[a]t he might reveal his image to the ru[l]ers in the universe. Rather, he came and displayed to the universe be[cause of h]is soul and his son, who is [dispersed in] every [place], that he might enable him to live [once more] and make for him a release; and to free (the soul) from every bond and all the fetters, in which it is entangled and bound.

Still, you, look and see! The rulers and the authorities, in that they had no form in [their world like] him, they lusted for his image. They reflected upon themselves, that [they] had no [one] like him in their creation. They sealed hi[s im]a[g]e in their heart, within their soul. Afterward[s, they] built it according to his likeness; they formed Adam and [Ev]e. They sealed the image of the exalted one in their [soul]. So, they [co]pied with an imitation; but they have not [copied i]n truth! Rather, just as [a form is copied from its model,] it is made as these, for [i]t came [from them,] but it is not l[ik]e him in truth. [Again, so too] is this figure of ma[nkind. They copi]ed it against the image of the exalted one [but it is not that image in truth.]
Similarly the [t]ree, for while it is like the [living tree, it is] not [copi]ed in truth.

This matt[er is comparable to] this: As a great, fre[e] woman [who dwells] within her [palace, who is] rich in wealth [and] po[ss]essions; she is also beautiful in her beauty, and is virtuous in her modesty. She walks in a free and reputable position. The fame of her beauty has spread in every c[i]ty. She sur[passes all others.] Behold h[er] chamber [that makes every] one who is mad, because [of] the nobles and the great ones. Al[so], they lust for her beautiful face. They did not [reach] her, because she is hidden in her palace [and dwells] within in a [secret place. None may] meet that woman [except] his so[n]; or rather the head [of t]hat garment. This free woman shall [then] leave the cha[mber] behind her and come to the street [and uncover] her head [openly,] and she reveals her [face and her beauty to all,] because of her beloved broth[er]. This wom[an], on whom no man ever looked, nor did they ever see her fa[ce], as she neither desires nor rejoices [in display, shall] leave her chamber behind her, and come in the midst of mankind [that all may behold her] and everyone view her. The hones[t] men and the nobles, even the servants too, and the [lowly ones,] look at her.

[Understa]nd also this other (matter) that I will teach you. For, [a]s with Adam and Eve, whom the rulers fashioned and [se]aled after the image of the exalted one, so too this [i]s how a manifold divinity and many powers and angels [also received] the stamp of that image, which was displayed to them. For, in the majesty of the l[ig]ht and (the image's) love, they glowed with their desire and they were undone. Th[ey] were eager for their lust; like a m[an who looks] to the majesty of a lusted after face, and [is consumed,] and he is eager for the [force] of the desire.

Now, this new birth that they begot in a new [manner] in the world, is Adam and Eve. [There is not a] form in their world since the beginning like it; because that [im]age [occ]urs not in the worlds b[el]ow.
Not all the figures that have been fashioned were fashioned by birth from displayed intercourse. Rather, there are other figures fashioned [by other means.]
One of them is the sea [gi]ant, the 'sweeping' from the sphere, which the [Father] of Life discharged into the sea. Its own fire and thought fashioned it [in] a figure.

The second figure is the one [that] fell to the earth. It made the sea its womb. Its own l[us]t became its sculptor. It alone fashioned it to a nature, which is the root of death. Yet, when it came up from the sea, it [sought] that it might destroy the works [of the Father] of Life. They immediately sent against it the Adamant of Light, the great 'instruction of vigour'. He humbled it in the districts of the north. He has trampled underfoot and set h[im]self upon it, until the end of the world.
[The] third figure is the nature that fell on wh[at] is dr[y. It] fashioned the tree and set itself there. [So this is the] new figure that was fashioned [from the ground and d]isplays.

So, in accord with the essence they [partake of the Dark]ness; but yet th[ey] did not come with the King of Dark[ness to the wo]rld. Rather, their fashioning [came] about [afterwards;] they are composite and have been displayed in the world.

In accord with this simile: Again, [this] too [is] how [ ... ] the Ambassador becomes [ ... ... ] as this free woman [ ... not] according to wantonness, in pride, nor [ ... she co]nsented to the outer world, she [ ... ... ], she revealed her face and her [beau]ty [ ... ] but only due to the constraint of grief [about] her [bel]ov[ed one].

Now, this too is the way of the Third Ambassador, when he came and display[ed his] image with a show towards all the powers. [He did] not [co]me so that all the rulers and the author[it]ies would sculpt a form [after h]is likeness. R[ather], he came because of his son being crucified in the totality; [fo]r he would release him, free him, and rescue him from oppres-sion. Yet, when the rulers looked o[n] him, [th]ey lusted for his image. They fashioned after his [like]ness Adam and Eve, without the consent of the gre[at]ness.

This is [als]o the case with those powers, when they looked on that majestic and beautiful [imag]e, they () [ ... ] a first image. They received the stamp of th[at image], which was displayed to them. They copied [ ... wh]ich th[ey co]pied out in a likeness, it being made [ ... ... ] the ones that they had put forth, which had received a [stamp of this im]age; but inward even to the rocks [ ... ... ] which occur from place to place. The [...] of that image, which was displayed in the universe [ ... ] they received a stamp, it being revealed there, and an impress.
